components.description: The same chip the Origin 200 uses, on the IO-8 assembly at PCI device 4. On the Origin 300 it exposes serial A and B, the parallel function, the byte-bus Timekeeper and the board's 10/100 Ethernet, and no keyboard or mouse controller. No rear-panel parallel connector is established by the reviewed IO-8 connector inventory. The chip includes its one-wire engine, but this board does not fit the IOC3 Ethernet-address identity part: the address comes from the brick EEPROM through the L1. Serial A is the guest console; serial B is the second rear-panel serial port. Emulator chardev index 0 is reserved for the separate L1 management channel, with IOC3 A and B on indexes 1 and 2. The integration contract uses explicit population mask 0x17 and selects M48T35-compatible timekeeper-kind 1 as a documented compatibility choice whose clearance depends on the required Origin 300 qtest.

identity.notes: Function 00:04.0 and PCI revision 1 are observed. The exact IP45 subsystem device field is not observed. The initial emulator retains the IOC3 class's public SGI subsystem vendor and exposes 0xffff as an explicit device placeholder so it does not inherit the Origin 200 system-board value 0xc303. An Origin 300 configuration-space capture replaces the placeholder.

components.description: The same chip the Origin 200 uses, on the IO-8 assembly at PCI device 4. On the Origin 300 it exposes serial A and B, the parallel function, the byte-bus Timekeeper and the board's 10/100 Ethernet, and no keyboard or mouse controller. No rear-panel parallel connector is established by the reviewed IO-8 connector inventory. The chip includes its one-wire engine, but this board does not fit the IOC3 Ethernet-address identity part: the address comes from the brick EEPROM through the L1. Serial A is the guest console; serial B is the second rear-panel serial port. Emulator chardev index 0 is reserved for the separate L1 management channel, with IOC3 A and B on indexes 1 and 2. The integration contract uses explicit population mask 0x17 and selects M48T35-compatible timekeeper-kind 1 as a documented compatibility choice whose clearance depends on the required Origin 300 qtest.

identity.notes: Function 00:04.0 and PCI revision 1 are observed. The exact IP45 subsystem device field is not observed. The initial emulator retains the IOC3 class's public SGI subsystem vendor and exposes 0xffff as an explicit device placeholder so it does not inherit the Origin 200 system-board value 0xc303. An Origin 300 configuration-space capture replaces the placeholder.

machine.name: Two-chassis Origin 300
machine.notes: Two Origin 300 servers cabled LINK connector to LINK connector over one NUMAlink 3 cable, with no router, as the User's Guide's "Connecting Two Servers" procedure builds it: the operator designates one server master and one slave, sets the slave's L1 to brick slot 02 so its module reads 001c02 above the master's 001c01, connects the console to the master and sets both L1s' network mode to 422. Each chassis is a complete base module, with its own IP45 node board, Bedrock, processors, memory, XBridge, IO-8 and L1; two posted direct-cabled pairs show every one of those per module (the OpenBSD list capture of 2014 and Nekochan thread 17314). The same cable carries the two L1s' RS-422 pair, which routes console and diagnostic data and propagates reset, NMI and power between the chassis (108-0240-002 printed page 2-47). This file fixes no NASID: the stock IP35 PROM numbers the nodes by discovery at every boot, and a routed pair's module 001c01 came up as NASID 1. The master and slave designation is the L1's, not a NASID. Planned: the QEMU family builder still refuses a second Bedrock node, so this topology is not exported to the emulator until the NUMAlink cable between two Bedrocks is modeled.

variants.notes: QEMU's currently shipping 500 MHz/2 MiB Origin 300 configuration writes this exact Config0 low-25-bit reset word (readback 0x6c9aa985), independently reviewed in docs/reviews/origin300-config0-reset-word-review.md and recorded in docs/datasheets/r14000.md. No product here yet reads this field; it moves machine.firmware_config.processor_reset_mode here for a future compiler once a Bedrock-node compile path exists. The complete Config0 write mask remains unestablished for R14000 (docs/datasheets/r14000.md), so only the literal word is carried, not a named-field encoding.

space_selection.notes: Unchanged from the Origin 200: two uncached-attribute bits the R10000-family processor drives beside the 40-bit physical address. The seven-space, address-field encoding this file once carried matches no public source, MIPS or Itanium; the Origin 200's two-bit emulation carrier therefore fits this generation as it stands.
